phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Line and zig-zag configurations differ in whether intermediate even-site population is strongly suppressed during transfer.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Conceptual population-flow schematic for line versus zig-zag state-transfer layouts.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Eq. (1) and surrounding text
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The state-transfer dynamics are modeled by a nearest-neighbor XY Hamiltonian with site frequencies ω_n and couplings J_n.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Hamiltonian matrix H for an N-site single-excitation chain with engineered onsite frequencies and nearest-neighbor hoppings.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Mirror-symmetric frequencies/couplings together with odd-π eigenvalue spacings are sufficient conditions for perfect state transfer, and the line configuration ω_n=0, J_n=(J/2)√(n(N-n)) realizes PST.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: PST parameter constraints plus the conventional line-configuration coupling law.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For odd N and integer m≥0, the zig-zag configuration with ω_n(m)=μ_n·2mJ and J_n(m)=(J/2)√([n+μ_n2m][N-n+μ_{n+1}2m]) satisfies the PST conditions.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Closed-form zig-zag frequency and coupling schedule generated from the chosen eigenvalue ladder λ(m).

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: At large m, even-site occupation vanishes and the zig-zag chain reduces to an effective half-length line chain with explicit ω_eff and J_eff, separated by an energy gap 2m in the positive spectrum.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Large-m effective odd-site Hamiltonian and its associated gapped eigenvalue pattern.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Fig. 2a and accompanying paragraphs
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: In the 1×3 chain, bright spots in the Q3 population map mark PST solutions, with the first four spots matching the m=0,1,2,3 zig-zag solutions and reaching Q3 population near unity.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Population heatmap P_Q3(J12,Δ;τ=60 ns) for the 3-site chain together with predicted PST loci for m=0..3.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The experimentally inferred J12/2π values agree with the analytic zig-zag predictions: about 6 vs 5.9 MHz for m=0 and about 10.2, 13.2, 15.6 MHz for m=1,2,3.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Analytic coupling values J12(m) for m=0..3 and their comparison targets against extracted bright-spot locations.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Increasing m suppresses even-site occupation in PST dynamics: the 1×3 fine scans evolve from fragmented to continuous structure and the 1×5 chain shows almost no even-site population by m=6.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Time-resolved population maps for 1×3 and 1×5 chains at different m values.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Fractional state transfer for remote entanglement is obtained by an isospectral deformation that rescales the two central couplings by cosθ±sinθ while keeping all other parameters unchanged.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Modified central couplings \tilde J_(N-1)/2 and \tilde J_(N+1)/2 used to produce FST from the PST chain.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Main text, Fig. 3a-d and surrounding paragraphs
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For N=5 and θ=π/8, FST produces endpoint populations near 0.5 and Bell-state fidelities 0.909±0.024 for m=0 and 0.925±0.021 for m=4, with stronger suppression of even-qubit population at larger m.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Five-qubit FST population traces plus two-qubit endpoint tomography and Bell-fidelity estimates for m=0 and m=4.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Under Gaussian frequency noise on even qubits, fidelity degradation is slower for larger m; at σ/2π=30 MHz the reported F/F0 values are 0.56, 0.66, and 0.85 for m=0,4,6.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Noise-robustness curve F/F0 versus σ for several zig-zag configurations.

phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The 2D 3×3 extension exhibits periodic corner-population transfer, reaches a four-corner W state at 56 ns, revives near 111 ns, and yields a reported W-state fidelity of 0.85.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Three-by-three network FST population evolution together with four-corner W-state tomography and ideal W-state reference.
